title: Early New Orleans drummers
summary: Walter Brunson, Mack Murray, Barbarin, Joe Lindsey, Black Benny, Zutty Singleton and John Vigne, with Bill Mathias's brother.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Mm-hmm. I wonder if there's anything else you can tell us about the early drummers when you were a boy, even before you took up music. You mentioned, of course, your teacher, Cantrell. Cantrell. But some of the other early drummers. Walter Brunson.
Yeah.
Walter Brunson. Yeah. Baby Dodd said he used to take lessons from him. He liked him.
He was good, yeah. Well, I know him a twine, there was no read. And one named Mack Murray.
Oh, Mack Murray.
Yeah.
Well, anything about Walter Brunson? Anything else about his style? What kind of a brother?

He was wonderful. He was wonderful. Had a fella named Mack Murray, too. Yeah. Well, Barbara and I, we about to start together. Paul Barbara. Yeah, we start about together. And we had a little fella by the name of your talk, Joe Lindsey. Oh, yeah, Joe Lindsey. Yeah, we was talking at the same time. I knew him.
He was a friend of Louis Armstrong. Louis Armstrong, yeah.
Yeah, yeah. Joe Lindsey.
I met him up in Chicago. Baby Dodds. Yeah.
Hendriss Eno.
Oh, yeah, I never knew him. I heard people talking.
Yeah, he was good too, Hendriss Eno. You remember who he played with? Well, he used to play all in my club, different band. And Black, we were talking Black Benny. Yeah. Little Red Happy.
Yeah, I never knew him either. I never knew Black Benny. I heard people talking.
I know all of them. Black Benny used to come and try to get lessons from me. And Zula Singleton. He's up Zula Singleton. Yeah, they call him Zula, yeah.
I knew him in New York.
Yeah, he left here.
Well, he used to talk about the John Veen. Do you remember?
John Veen, oh, he's an old man.
Yeah.

Well, I remember I took his job. He'd sleep. He had a shop in the daytime and sleep all night. Yeah, I remember. Yeah, a long time. I had a, what you call him playing at that time too? Sidney Bechet. Sidney Bechet. I know Sidney Bechet. Well, yeah. That was one of them nightclubs, you know, then. He'd sleep all day. John Veen, he's there. He used to play bass on the parade. A bass drum. Yeah, the parade, yeah. What bands did he play with?
Well, all them bands, like Imperial Band, you know.
Yeah. Yeah. Now, you got a fella playing trombone. His brother was a drummer too. From Al Jays. They called his brother Bebe, Bill Mathias. Oh, yeah.
He had a brother play drums, Bebe.
Yeah, I heard it.
I never knew it. I know Bill. Yeah, Bill played. He used to play drum too, but he played trombone.
